changes.speaker: Chanel
changes.source_note: Japanese is the blunt insult きさまっ..., stronger and more masculine-coded than neutral 'you'.

changes.speaker: Chanel
changes.before: The logic of division of labor. I shall eat California oranges at a heated table.
changes.after: That's the logic of division of labor. I'll be eating California oranges at a heated table.
changes.source_note: Japanese uses casual ～だよ and わたし; 'I shall' makes Chanel implausibly formal.

changes.speaker: Old Karl
changes.before: Come, everyone, back to your rooms. He needs rest.
changes.after: Come now. Why don't the rest of you return to your rooms? He needs his rest.
changes.source_note: Japanese uses elderly みなの衆 and ～じゃ, with a gentler suggestion rather than a clipped command.

changes.speaker: Old Karl
changes.before: Here, the answer is a person.
changes.after: In this case, the answer is clearly a person, you see.
changes.source_note: Japanese ends in elderly ～じゃの; the English gains a light old-scholar cadence without caricature.

changes.speaker: Dunant
changes.before: Ashby was still young. A spy who used bombs was something unheard of.
changes.after: Ashby was still green. Who'd ever heard of a spy using bombs?
changes.source_note: Japanese calls Ashby 青二才 (a green youngster) and frames bomb-using spies as something one would never hear of; this restores Dunant's hard-boiled veteran register.

changes.speaker: Stra
changes.after: A creator, that's who! Any complaints?
changes.source_note: Japanese self-grandiosely says クリエイター様だ; the stronger English matches Stra's theatrical persona without inventing an accent.

changes.speaker: Tianon
changes.before: Oh? You seem troubled...allow me to tell your fortune.
changes.after: Oh? You seem troubled...allow me to divine your fortune.
changes.source_note: 占ってしんぜましょう is gracious and slightly archaic; 'divine' preserves Tianon's elegant mystical register.

changes.speaker: Tianon
changes.before: ...the least suspicious person is the most suspicious...how's that for a theory?
changes.after: ...the least suspicious person is the most suspicious...that is what I see.
changes.source_note: Japanese こんナンでましたケド presents the result of her divination; 'how's that for a theory?' makes her sound flippant rather than mystical.

notes.method: Direct visual review of the retail-Japanese rendered dialogue, followed by exact verification against the current post-correction canonical branch.
notes.scope: Only explicit register mismatches are changed. No phonetic accents, ethnic caricatures, or blanket pseudo-Edwardian rewriting.
notes.unchanged_cast: Lumeranka, Ruthie, Braque, Fitz, Captain, crew, Navigator, Bosun, Ship's Doctor, Fred, and Locke were reviewed and left unchanged because the current English already carries their source register adequately.
notes.punctuation: ASCII punctuation and the project's compact ellipsis style are preserved.
